observation_summary: The Base32 codec throws an IllegalArgumentException when using 'W' as a padding character with the hex alphabet, because 'W' is incorrectly included in the HEX_DECODE_TABLE.
hypothesis: The HEX_DECODE_TABLE contains an extra entry (32) that maps to a character which should not be part of the valid Base32 hex alphabet, causing the validation logic to incorrectly identify 'W' as being in the alphabet.
prediction: Removing the erroneous value '32' from the HEX_DECODE_TABLE array will allow 'W' to be used as a padding character, as it will no longer be considered part of the alphabet.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of the value '32' from the HEX_DECODE_TABLE array. This confirms that the issue was an incorrect initialization of the lookup table used for alphabet validation.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect value in a static lookup table (HEX_DECODE_TABLE). This is a classic Assignment/Initialization defect where the state of the object (the table) was initialized with an incorrect value, leading to incorrect behavior in the validation logic. It is not a Checking bug because the validation logic itself is correct; it is not an Algorithm/Method bug because the procedure is correct; it is not a Function/Class/Object bug because it is a local data initialization error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The validation logic (isInAlphabet) is correct; the problem is that the data it relies on (the table) is initialized incorrectly.
The procedure for checking the alphabet is correct; the issue is the data structure being checked.
